newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine rejects civil service charges.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine rejects civil service charges.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine denied on Sunday that the ruling Conservatives had tried to use the neutral civil service for party political ends.

Newspapers reported on Sunday that Sir Robin Butler, the head of the civil service, had vetoed an order to officials to draw up a list of businessmen who had won government contracts and who would publicly back Conservative policies.

Heseltine dismissed the reports as a smear campaign by the Labour Party. "There is absolutely no possible interpretation of what has happened over the last 24 hours than it has been part of the Labour Party's dirty tricks campaign," he told the BBC.
Heseltine said the matter had been dealt with in the summer.

"I agreed with the head of the civil service Sir Robin Butler that the matter must be clear and there must be no question of civil servants being expected to be doing anything that could be seen to be party political.
"That is the position I have always taken and that matter was dealt with in the summer," Heseltine said.
By law the British civil service must remain politically neutral. The reports said the idea of the list had been proposed by Heseltine in a letter which was leaked to the media.
Liz Symonds, general secretary of the Association of First Division Civil Servants which represents senior officials, said she was delighted the idea had been overruled.
Other officials were quoted by the Sunday Times newspaper saying the decision by Butler to veto the request was unusual.

Labour seized on the report, arguing that the idea showed the government, which is lagging Labour in the polls with less than six months before an election, was sleaze-ridden. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7947
